questions.problem:
Find the radius of curvature for the curve $r(t)$ at the point $r(\pi )$ if the curve and the derivative ${T}^{′}(t)$ of the corresponding unit tangent vector are given by

$$
r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,4,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩,\,{T}^{′}(t)=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the curve $r(t)$ and the derivative ${T}^{′}(t)$ of the unit tangent, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

First, we find ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\pi ),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate ${T}^{′}(\pi )$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the radius of curvature at $r(\pi )$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=\frac{1}{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that  its  unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,\frac{3}{5}⟩\,.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature: 

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\frac{4}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{3}{5})⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{4}{5}\cdot \frac{2}{5}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,-\frac{4}{5}(-\frac{2}{5}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})),\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{8}{25}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,\frac{8}{25}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{8}{25}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}),\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{8}{25}\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{2s}{5}))}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{8}{25}\sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{2s}{5})} \\  & =\frac{8}{25}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{8}{25})}=\frac{25}{8}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡s,\,\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡s),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{2}\operatorname{cos}⁡s)⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡s,\,-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\operatorname{cos}⁡s)}^{2}+{(-\sqrt{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡s)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{{cos}^{2}⁡s+{cos}^{2}⁡s+2{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2{cos}^{2}⁡s+2{sin}^{2}⁡s} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2({cos}^{2}⁡s+{sin}^{2}⁡s)} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\cdot \sqrt{2} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{1}=1.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
T(s)=\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\sqrt{3}⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\sqrt{3})⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨-\frac{\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s}}{2\sqrt{s}},\,0⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s},\,\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s},\,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\cdot \sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡\sqrt{s})}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡\sqrt{s})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\cdot \sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡\sqrt{s}+{cos}^{2}⁡\sqrt{s}} \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\cdot 1 \\  & =\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{4\sqrt{s}})}=4\sqrt{s}.
$$

questions.problem:
Consider a curve $r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that  its  unit tangent vector $T(s)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i+\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j+\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3}\,k\,.\end{aligned}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since the curve $r(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature: 

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{κ(s)}=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}
$$

We differentiate $T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))\,j+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\frac{\sqrt{5}}{3})k \\  & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{3}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))\,i+\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j+0\,k \\  & =-\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i+\frac{2}{9}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j \\  & =\frac{2}{9}[-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j] \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{{(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}\sqrt{{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3})+{cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3})} \\  & =\frac{2}{9}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s)=\frac{1}{‖{T}^{′}(s)‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{2}{9})}=\frac{9}{2}.
$$

questions.problem: Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(3,1)$ where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$, given that $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖=2,$ and the unit tangent vector to the curve is $\,T(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(\frac{\pi }{2})=⟨3,1⟩,$ since the point $P(3,1)$ is at the tip of $r(\frac{\pi }{2}).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩=⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩=⟨-1,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{2}{1}=2.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})}{‖{T}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=⟨-1,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\frac{\pi }{2})+R(\frac{\pi }{2})N(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨3,1⟩+2⟨-1,0⟩=⟨1,1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

The center is $(0,0)$ and the radius is $1$

questions.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $r(t)$ at the point $P(\pi ,2)$ where $t=\pi $, given that $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖=2,$ and the unit tangent vector $T(t)$ to the curve is

$$
T(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2}),\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2})⟩.
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(\pi )=⟨\pi ,2⟩$,  since the point $P(\pi ,2)$ is at the tip of $r(\pi ).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t),$ ${T}^{′}(\pi )$ and $‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2})),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2}))⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{t}{2}),-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{t}{2})⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(\pi ) & =\frac{1}{2}⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})⟩=\frac{1}{2}⟨0,-1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\frac{1}{2}\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{(-1)}^{2}}=\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=\frac{2}{(\frac{1}{2})}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t=\pi $ as

$$
\begin{aligned}N(\pi ) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(\pi )}{‖{T}^{′}(\pi )‖}=\frac{(\frac{1}{2})}{(\frac{1}{2})}⟨0,-1⟩=⟨0,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(\pi )+R(\pi )N(\pi ) & =⟨\pi ,2⟩+4⟨0,-1⟩=⟨\pi ,-2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t)$, we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(0)=⟨0,0⟩,$ since the point $P(0,0)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$ 

Now, we find ${T}^{′}(t)$, ${T}^{′}(0)$ and $‖{T}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the radius of curvature is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{1} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)+R(0)N(0) & =⟨0,0⟩+1\cdot ⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0⟩+⟨1,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,0⟩.\end{aligned}

$$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the value of $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖$ and the unit tangent $T(t),$ we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(t)‖}
$$

Notice that $r(0)=⟨1,0⟩,$ since the point $P(1,0)$ is at the tip of $r(0).$

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {T}^{′}(0) & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡0-\operatorname{cos}⁡0,\operatorname{cos}⁡0-\operatorname{sin}⁡0⟩=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}⟨-1,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cdot \sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{\sqrt{2}}{1}=\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}

$$

$$

questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(0),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(0)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4t)⟩ \\  & =⟨8t,\,4⟩ \\  & =4⟨2t,\,1⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =4⟨2(0),\,1⟩ \\  & =4⟨0,\,1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =4\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =4⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =4⟨2,\,0⟩ \\  & =8⟨1,\,0⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =8⟨1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(0)$ and ${r}^{″}(0)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =4⟨0,\,1,\,0⟩\times 8⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =32\,\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =32\,\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-32k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =32\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖} \\  & =\frac{{4}^{3}}{32} \\  & =\frac{64}{32} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\pi $ for the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t),$ we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,{e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t)⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨{e}^{\pi }(\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi -\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ),\,{e}^{\pi }(\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi )⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{\pi },\,-{e}^{\pi }⟩ \\  & ={e}^{\pi }⟨-1,\,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & ={e}^{\pi }\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}=\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t+\operatorname{cos}⁡t))⟩ \\  & =⟨-2{e}^{t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,2{e}^{t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =⟨-2{e}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,2{e}^{\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & ={e}^{\pi }⟨0,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and ${r}^{″}(\pi )$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi ) & ={e}^{\pi }⟨-1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times {e}^{\pi }⟨0,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & ={({e}^{\pi })}^{2}\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & -1 & 0 \\ \,0 & -2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & ={e}^{2\pi }\cdot \left|\begin{aligned}-1 & -1 \\ \,0 & -2\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2{e}^{2\pi }\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖ & =2{e}^{2\pi }\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi ){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖}=\frac{{(\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\pi })}^{3}}{\,2{e}^{2\pi }\,}=\sqrt{2}\,{e}^{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,2,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =2\end{aligned}

$$

questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\pi $ for the curve $r(t)=⟨{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t},\,{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t)$, ${r}^{′}(\pi ),$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖$:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\pi ) & =⟨{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{0},\,-{e}^{-1}\cdot 0⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,\,0⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )‖ & =\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+0}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡t}{cos}^{2}⁡t,\,-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t+{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡t}{sin}^{2}⁡t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =⟨-{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi +{e}^{\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi }{cos}^{2}⁡\pi ,\,-{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi }\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi +{e}^{\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi }{sin}^{2}⁡\pi ⟩ \\  & =⟨0+1,{e}^{-1}+0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\frac{1}{e}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\pi )$ and ${r}^{″}(\pi )$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi ) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩\times ⟨1,\,\frac{1}{e},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -1 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & 1/e & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1/e\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-\frac{1}{e}\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖ & =\frac{1}{e}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=\pi $ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\pi ) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(\pi ){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\pi )\times {r}^{″}(\pi )‖}=\frac{1}{(\frac{1}{e})}=e.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ for the curve $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩.$
questions.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $r(t)$, we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t)=\frac{1}{κ(t)}=\frac{‖{r}^{′}(t){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(t)\times {r}^{″}(t)‖}
$$

First, we calculate ${r}^{′}(t),$ ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and $‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,-2⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+(-2)^{2}}=2\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we calculate ${r}^{″}(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=\frac{\pi }{2}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2\operatorname{cos}⁡2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,-4\operatorname{sin}⁡2t⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2}),-4\operatorname{sin}⁡(2\cdot \frac{\pi }{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the cross product by considering ${r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ and ${r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =⟨0,\,-2,\,0⟩\times ⟨-1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & -2 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}0 & \,\,-2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =-2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

  

Therefore, the radius of the osculating circle at  $t=\frac{\pi }{2}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(\frac{\pi }{2}) & =\frac{{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(\frac{\pi }{2})\times {r}^{″}(\frac{\pi }{2})‖}=\frac{{2}^{3}}{\,2\,}=4.\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Consider a curve $\mathbf r(s)$ parametrized by its arc length $s.$ Find the radius of curvature of $\mathbf r(s)$ at an arbitrary point knowing that  its  unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(s)$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}T(s) & =-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i+\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j\,.\end{aligned}
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since the curve $\mathbf{r}(s)$ and its unit tangent vector $\mathbf T(s)$ are both parametrized by arc length $s,$ we will use the following formula for the radius of curvature:

$$
R(s) = \dfrac{1}{\kappa(s)} = \dfrac{1}{\|\mathbf T'(s)\|}
$$

We differentiate $\mathbf T(s)$ with respect to $s$ and calculate its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(s) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}s}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))\,j \\  & =-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,i-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3})\,j \\ ‖{T}^{′}(s)‖ & =\sqrt{(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))^{2}+(-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{9}({cos}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3})+{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{s}{3}))} \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore, the radius of curvature is

$$
R(s) = \dfrac{1}{\|\mathbf T'(s)\|} = \dfrac{1}{\:\dfrac{1}{3}\:} = 3\,.
$$

canonical_examples.problem:
Find the center and radius of the osculating circle to the curve $\mathbf{r}(t)$ at the point $\mathbf{r}(0),$ if the curve and the derivative $\mathbf{T}'(t)$ of the corresponding unit tangent vector are given by

 

$$
\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle t, \:\dfrac{ t^2}{2}\right\rangle, \qquad \mathbf T'(t)= \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{(t^2+1)^3}}\left\langle -t, \:  1\right\rangle \,.
$$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since we are given both the curve $\mathbf{r}(t)$ and the derivative $\mathbf T'(t)$ of the unit tangent, we will use the following formula to compute the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t) = \dfrac{1}{\mathbf \kappa(t)} = \dfrac{\| \mathbf r'(t) \|}{\left\| \mathbf T'(t) \right\|}
$$

First, we find $\mathbf{r}'(t),$ $\mathbf r'(0),$ and $\|\mathbf r'(0)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨1,t⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨1,0⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we evaluate $\mathbf T'(0)$ and find its magnitude:

$$
\begin{aligned}{T}^{′}(0) & =⟨-\frac{0}{\sqrt{(1+{0}^{2})^{3}}},\,\frac{1}{\sqrt{(1+{0}^{2})^{3}}}⟩=⟨0,1⟩ \\ ‖{T}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{{0}^{2}+{1}^{2}}=1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature is 

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0)‖}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=\frac{1}{1}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we find the principal normal vector at $t = 0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}N(0) & =\frac{{T}^{′}(0)}{‖{T}^{′}(0)‖}=⟨0,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the center of the osculating circle is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0)+R(0)N(0) & = \\ ⟨0,0⟩+1\cdot ⟨0,1⟩ & = \\ ⟨0,1⟩ & .\end{aligned}
$$

canonical_examples.problem: Find the radius of the osculating circle at the point where $t=0$ for the curve $\mathbf r(t)=\left\langle e^{ t}, \: e^{- t} \right\rangle.$
canonical_examples.worked_solution:
Since we are given only the curve $\mathbf r(t),$ we will use the cross product formula to find the radius of curvature:

$$
R(t) = \dfrac{1}{\kappa(t)} = \dfrac{\|\mathbf r'(t)\|^3}{\left\|\mathbf r'(t) \times \mathbf r''(t) \right\|}
$$

First, we calculate $\mathbf r'(t),$ $\mathbf r'(0),$ and $\|\mathbf r'(0)\|\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{′}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,-1⟩ \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)‖ & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we calculate $\mathbf r''(t)$ and evaluate it at $t=0\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{″}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(-{e}^{-t})⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,{e}^{-t}⟩ \\ {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,{e}^{-0}⟩ \\  & =⟨1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the cross product by considering $\mathbf r'(0)$ and $\mathbf r''(0)$ as $3$-dimensional vectors with zero $z$-components:

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,0⟩\times ⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & \,-1 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & \,-1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =2\,k \\ ‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖ & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the radius of curvature at $t=0$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}R(0) & =\frac{‖{r}^{′}(0){‖}^{3}}{‖{r}^{′}(0)\times {r}^{″}(0)‖}=\frac{{(\sqrt{2})}^{3}}{\,2\,}=\sqrt{2}\,.\end{aligned}
$$
